title: The true person of no rank
hookLine: Linji: a true person of no rank goes in and out of your face

cards: Name tags at a conference. Doctor, director, intern, guest. Titles on the email signature, ranks on the uniform.
On any given day a person carries a few of them, and they do real work: they tell people who to ask and what to expect.

A Chan teacher named Linji once stood in front of his assembly and pointed at something none of those titles reach. He said it lives right here, in this lump of flesh, and comes and goes through the doors of your face.
He gave it a name. Today, Linji.

teach.h: A TRUE PERSON OF NO RANK.
teach.b: First, the sermon. In the Record of Linji, he climbs to the teaching seat and says, roughly: on your lump of red flesh there is a true person of no rank, always going in and out through the gates of your face.
Those who haven't seen it yet, look, look. Rank here means a place in the order of things: high or low, monk or lay, teacher or student. The true person has none.
Second, the challenge. A monk steps forward and asks, what is this true person of no rank?
Linji comes down from the seat, grabs him, and says, speak, speak!

teach.h: THE MONK REACHES FOR AN ANSWER.
teach.b: The monk hesitates, reaching for the right answer. Linji pushes him away with a blunt insult and goes back to his room. Third, why so rough.
The monk had turned the true person into a topic, something to be defined. Linji wanted him to show it, right then, in his own seeing and hearing and speaking.
The moment he went looking for a correct reply, he had put the rank back on. Fourth, an ordinary Tuesday. You can be a manager, a parent, a patient, a beginner.
Those roles matter, and Linji isn't asking you to throw them away.
He is pointing at whatever is looking out of your eyes before any of the labels arrive. It hears the kettle the same way whether you're the boss or the new hire. That one, Linji says, has no rank.

how: Linji's sayings are studied in the Rinzai Zen tradition, which takes its name from him, and the true person of no rank appears among the koans that teachers give students to work on in meditation and interviews.

o: a ranking of monks by years since ordination
a Chan teacher who spoke of the true person of no rank
a Chinese title for the head of a monastery

high or low, monk or lay

s: Linji told his listeners to throw away their roles
he pointed at what is there before the roles; he didn't ask anyone to abandon them.
the monk got a gentle explanation
Linji grabbed him, said speak, and pushed him away.
Linji said the true person goes in and out through the face
seeing, hearing, speaking: right here, already.

games.q: Linji grabs you and says, speak, speak! about the true person of no rank. what do you do?
o: hesitate and search for the right answer
answer from right here, without reaching
games.why: the monk in the story hesitated, and Linji pushed him away. what he was asking for was a living response, not a definition.

practice: Say silently one label you carry, your job, your role at home, how good or bad you are at something, and feel how it sits on you.
Then set it to one side for a few breaths: hear the sounds in the room, feel the air at the nostrils, and notice that the hearing and the breathing don't need the title to work.

wordCard.voice: Linji. The Chan teacher who pointed to the true person of no rank, seeing and hearing through your face before any title arrives. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese wu wei zhen ren: true person with no rank, no position.

carryVoice: Your line: no rank. What looks out of your eyes wears no title. Day nine hundred eighty-nine, done.

sources.ref: Record of Linji (Linji lu), the 'true person of no rank' sermon
